messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Combinatorial-geometric: design via repeated affine-regular hexagons and strip arguments controlling all collinearity widths

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "Arrange 12 points as two concentric, rotationally offset affine-regular hexagons inscribed in the unit square (each hexagon affinely stretched to touch the square boundary), with the 13th point at the square's center; choosing the inner hexagon at scale ratio 1/3 and angular offset 30° relative to the outer, all 286 triangle areas are bounded below by 1/84 via strip-width arguments showing every line through two points leaves perpendicular distance at least 1/13 from some third point. The collinearity-width analysis decomposes into three strip families (outer-outer, inner-inner, cross-hexagon), each controlled by the affine-regular structure ensuring minimum strip widths of 3s/4, s/4, and s/6 respectively, where s is the outer hexagon's minimum side-length after the maximal area-preserving affine map into the unit square."}
